rule: Every resolved place remains selectable with its canonical score; only independently worthwhile settlements scoring 60 or more appear as town markers. Isolated castles and nature reserves are not transferred into settlement scores.
namingDecisions: Middle Drum resolves to Middle Drums.
The contextual Millden request resolves to Milldens near Balgavies, distinct from Millden Lodge in Glen Esk.
Netherton resolves to the eastern hamlet near Careston and Mains of Melgund, not Netherton by Memus.
Burnside resolves to Burnside of Rescobie, not Burnside of Duntrune.
Dubton resolves to the Guthrie-area hamlet, not the Hillside or Brechin properties.

additions.rationale: Careston Castle is retained as a named heritage property, not promoted as a tourist town or public attraction without verified visitor access.
Aldbar Castle is an archaeological property reference rather than an independently visitable settlement or confirmed public attraction.
This resolves to the eastern Netherton near Melgund and Careston, not Netherton by Memus; it has no independent destination-scale visitor offer.
Mains of Melgund is a mapped farm locality; Melgund Castle and estate heritage do not turn it into a tourist settlement.
Aberlemno has genuine village character, but the nationally important stones are a separate attraction and do not by themselves justify a 60+ town marker.
Pitkennedy remains selectable as a named hamlet without borrowing interest from Aberlemno or the wider cycle route.
Turin is a small rural locality; Turin Hill and surrounding heritage remain separate landscape or attraction evidence.
The requested spelling resolves to Rescobie. The hamlet has local character, while Rescobie Loch and its wildlife interest remain a separate visitor proposition.
Reswallie is retained independently and does not inherit the visitor value of Rescobie Loch or Forfar.
This resolves to Burnside of Rescobie, centred on Burnside House, rather than the unrelated Burnside of Duntrune.
Balgavies is retained as a hamlet; the loch wildlife reserve is a separate attraction and does not inflate the settlement score.
The contextual request resolves to Milldens near Balgavies, represented from West Milldens, and is distinct from Millden and Millden Lodge in Glen Esk.
The requested singular spelling resolves to mapped Middle Drums, a small rural locality rather than a visitor destination.
This resolves to the Dubton west of Glasterlaw and Guthrie, not the separate properties near Hillside or Brechin.
Glasterlaw is a recognisable mapped hamlet but does not currently support an independent visitor-town experience.
The requested spelling resolves to Guthrie. Its village and heritage character are genuine, while Guthrie Castle remains private and does not support a 60+ score.
Kinnell has a distinct village and kirk setting but too little independently verified visitor depth for the town map.
